content: Ammonium ferric citrate is a food additive identified by the E number E381, primarily used as an acidity regulator. It appears as a green or reddish-brown powder that is highly soluble in water. The molecular formula of ammonium iron(III) citrate is not fixed and can vary. It is synthesized by combining ferric hydroxide (Fe(OH)3) with an aqueous solution of citric acid and ammonia. The compound typically contains 5–16% iron and approximately 75% hydrated citric acid. The green form of ammonium ferric citrate is more susceptible to reduction by light compared to the brown form. Beyond its role as a food additive, ammonium ferric citrate has several other applications. It is used in water purification processes and in the production of cyanotype prints, a photographic printing method. In this context, it acts as a reducing agent for metal salts with low activity, such as gold and silver. It is also a key component in a widely used cyanotype recipe that involves potassium ferricyanide. In microbiology, ammonium ferric citrate is utilized in Kligler iron agar to detect hydrogen sulfide production during microbial metabolism. Additionally, it is an ingredient in the Scottish carbonated soft drink Irn-Bru. In the field of medicine, ammonium ferric citrate serves as a contrast medium for imaging purposes. It is also employed as a hematinic, a substance used to treat or prevent iron-deficiency anemia.
